slides.headline: What does it mean?
slides.body: A loan term is the agreed length of time you have to repay a facility in full. Shorter terms generally mean higher regular repayments but less interest paid overall, while longer terms lower repayments but typically increase the total interest cost across the life of the loan.

bullet_points: Shorter terms mean higher repayments, less total interest
Longer terms mean lower repayments, more total interest
Term length is often matched to the funded asset or purpose
Terms can range from months to several years

caption:
Loan term is one of the biggest levers affecting how a facility feels day to day. A shorter term clears the debt faster and costs less in total interest, but the repayments are higher. A longer term eases monthly cash flow but adds to the total cost over time.

There's no universally "right" term — it depends on what the funds are being used for and how the business's cash flow is likely to look across that period.
